title: Neurocomputational Training to Improve Reward Responsiveness in Veterans With Anhedonia
official: Neurocomputational Training to Improve Reward Responsiveness in Veterans With Anhedonia
summary: Anhedonia, a reduction in motivation and in the ability to feel positive emotions, is widespread among Veterans across a range of psychiatric disorders. This impairment is associated with poorer psychosocial functioning and is resistant to first-line medication and psychotherapy treatments. However, interventions to improve anhedonia are sorely lacking. Reward learning supports motivation to seek rewards, and this mechanism can be enhanced by engaging in reward exploration. Our preliminary findings suggest that this approach can help improve reward responsiveness and positive mood among depressed and anxious individuals. Thus, the proposed research will test the preliminary efficacy of a computerized reward learning training in improving reward sensitivity and reducing anhedonia in Veterans. This new intervention could offer a novel remotely accessible treatment and help enhance the efficacy of existing evidence-based treatments for depression and other psychiatric conditions in Veterans.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* being a Veteran
* having at least moderate levels anhedonia (Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale score\>=20)
* having sufficient vision and reading skills to complete the study protocol
* being willing to attend treatment and assessment sessions

Exclusion Criteria:

* lifetime history of psychotic or bipolar I disorder
* neurological/neurodevelopmental disorders or sensory deficits that may impact cognitive function to preclude completion of study procedure (including past loss of consciousness \> 24 hours)
* taking certain psychotropic medications that may impact goal-directed task performance (e.g., benzodiazepines, sedative hypnotics); pre-existing stable doses (same regimen for at least 30 days) of psychotropic medications, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), will be allowed
* recent (past 3 months) or current severe alcohol or substance use disorder necessitating prioritization of substance use treatment
* recent (past month) or current risk of suicidal/homicidal behavior necessitating urgent higher level of care
* undergoing concurrent neuromodulation or cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy targeting depression, anhedonia, and/or PTSD
